requirements.title: Interpret stream as connection without multiplexing
requirements.statement: When the HTTP version in use does not support multiplexing streams, a reference to "stream" in this document MUST represent the entire connection.

requirements.title: Limit URI Template level
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be a level 3 template or lower.

requirements.title: Require absolute URI Template form
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be in absolute form.

requirements.title: Require non-empty URI Template components
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST include non-empty scheme, authority, and path components.

requirements.title: Start path with slash
requirements.statement: The path component of the URI Template MUST start with a slash ("/").

requirements.title: Keep template variables in path or query
requirements.statement: All template variables MUST be within the path or query components of the URI.

requirements.title: Allow other template variables
requirements.statement: The URI Template MAY contain other variables.

requirements.title: Require target_host and target_port
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST contain the variables "target_host" and "target_port".

requirements.title: Disallow non-ASCII characters
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT contain any non-ASCII Unicode characters.

requirements.title: Restrict URI Template to printable ASCII
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST only contain characters in the ASCII range 0x21-0x7E inclusive.

requirements.title: Disallow dot-prefix label expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Label Expansion with Dot-Prefix.

requirements.title: Disallow fragment expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Fragment Expansion ("#" operator).

requirements.title: Disallow reserved expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Reserved Expansion ("+" operator).

requirements.title: Disallow semicolon-prefix path-style parameter expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Path-Style Parameter Expansion with Semicolon-Prefix.

requirements.title: Disallow slash-prefix path segment expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Path Segment Expansion with Slash-Prefix.

requirements.title: Allow general-purpose URI Template implementations
requirements.statement: Clients MAY use a general-purpose URI Template implementation that lacks this specific validation.

requirements.title: Recommend validating URI Template requirements
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD validate the URI Template requirements above.

requirements.title: Reject invalid URI Template configuration
requirements.statement: If a client detects that any of the requirements above are not met by a URI Template, the client MUST reject its configuration and abort the request without sending it to the UDP proxy.

requirements.title: Allow constrained clients to use the default template
requirements.statement: Clients constrained by such limitations MAY attempt to access UDP proxying capabilities using the default template `https://$PROXY_HOST:$PROXY_PORT/.well-known/masque/udp/{target_host}/{target_port}/`.

requirements.title: Recommend offering service at the default template location
requirements.statement: UDP proxy deployments SHOULD offer service at this location if they need to interoperate with such clients.

requirements.title: Use HTTP Datagrams in the Section 5 format
requirements.statement: UDP tunnels MUST use HTTP Datagrams in the format defined in Section 5.

requirements.title: Use the Capsule Protocol for UDP tunnels
requirements.statement: UDP tunnels MUST use the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Initiate a UDP tunnel with the connect-udp token
requirements.statement: A client MUST issue a request containing the `connect-udp` upgrade token to initiate a UDP tunnel associated with a single HTTP stream.

requirements.title: Disallow IPv6 scoped addressing zone identifiers
requirements.statement: The `target_host` variable MUST NOT use IPv6 scoped addressing zone identifiers.

requirements.title: Adhere to the Figure 2 format for target_host and target_port
requirements.statement: The `target_host` and `target_port` variables MUST adhere to the format in Figure 2, using notation from ABNF.

requirements.title: Require a non-empty target_host
requirements.statement: The `target_host` variable MUST NOT be empty.

requirements.title: Require a non-empty target_port
requirements.statement: The `target_port` variable MUST NOT be empty.

requirements.title: Percent-encode IPv6 literal colons in target_host
requirements.statement: If `target_host` contains an IPv6 literal, the colons (`:`) MUST be percent-encoded.

requirements.title: Constrain target_port to the valid port range
requirements.statement: `target_port` MUST represent an integer between 1 and 65535 inclusive.

requirements.title: Target host syntax
requirements.statement: The `target_host` value MUST be an IPv6address, an IPv4address, or a reg-name.

requirements.title: Target port syntax
requirements.statement: The `target_port` value MUST be a port.

requirements.title: Expand URI template for request path and query
requirements.statement: When sending its UDP proxying request, the client SHALL perform URI Template expansion to determine the path and query of its request.

requirements.title: Convert HTTP Datagrams and UDP packets after a successful request
requirements.statement: If the request is successful, the UDP proxy MUST convert received HTTP Datagrams into UDP packets and UDP packets into HTTP Datagrams until the tunnel is closed.

requirements.title: Requests carry no message content
requirements.statement: UDP proxying requests MUST NOT carry any message content.

requirements.title: Successful responses carry no message content
requirements.statement: Successful UDP proxying responses MUST NOT carry any message content.

requirements.title: Reconstruct URI and open UDP tunnel
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy MUST extract target_host and target_port from the URI reconstructed from the request headers, decode their percent-encoding, and open a UDP socket to the requested target.

requirements.title: Respond before target packet
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy MUST respond to the request without waiting for a packet from the target.

requirements.title: Resolve DNS names before replying
requirements.statement: If target_host is a DNS name, the UDP proxy MUST perform DNS resolution before replying to the HTTP request.

requirements.title: Reject request on errors
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the UDP proxy MUST reject the request.

requirements.title: Send Proxy-Status details on errors
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the UDP proxy SHOULD send details using an appropriate Proxy-Status header field [PROXY-STATUS].

requirements.title: Validate source address on non-connected sockets
requirements.statement: If the UDP proxy uses a non-connected socket, it MUST validate the IP source address on received packets to ensure they match the client's request.

requirements.title: Validate source port on non-connected sockets
requirements.statement: If the UDP proxy uses a non-connected socket, it MUST validate the UDP source port on received packets to ensure they match the client's request.

requirements.title: Discard unmatched packets
requirements.statement: Packets that do not match MUST be discarded by the UDP proxy.

requirements.title: Keep socket open while request stream is open
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy MUST keep the socket open while the request stream is open.

requirements.title: Close request stream when socket is unusable
requirements.statement: If a UDP proxy is notified by its operating system that its socket is no longer usable, it MUST close the request stream.

requirements.title: Allow closing sockets after inactivity
requirements.statement: UDP proxies MAY choose to close sockets due to a period of inactivity.

requirements.title: Close request stream when closing socket
requirements.statement: When closing the socket, UDP proxies MUST close the request stream.

requirements.title: Avoid short inactivity timeouts
requirements.statement: UDP proxies that close sockets after a period of inactivity SHOULD NOT use a period lower than two minutes.

requirements.title: Abort request on non-success response
requirements.statement: Any response other than a successful response indicates that the request has failed; thus, the client MUST abort the request.

requirements.title: Avoid IP fragmentation for HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: UDP proxies MUST NOT introduce fragmentation at the IP layer when forwarding HTTP Datagrams onto a UDP socket.

requirements.title: Silently drop oversized datagrams
requirements.statement: UDP proxies MUST silently drop overly large datagrams when forwarding HTTP Datagrams onto a UDP socket.

requirements.title: Set IPv4 DF bit when possible
requirements.statement: In IPv4, the Don't Fragment (DF) bit MUST be set, if possible, to prevent fragmentation on the path.

requirements.title: Use GET method
requirements.statement: The method SHALL be "GET".

requirements.title: Include a single Host header field
requirements.statement: The request MUST include a single Host header field containing the origin of the UDP proxy.

requirements.title: Include Connection header field value Upgrade
requirements.statement: The request MUST include a Connection header field with value "Upgrade", compared case-insensitively.

requirements.title: Include Upgrade header field value connect-udp
requirements.statement: The request MUST include an Upgrade header field with value "connect-udp".

requirements.title: Respond with an error to malformed requests
requirements.statement: The recipient of such a malformed request MUST respond with an error.

requirements.title: Use 400 Bad Request for malformed requests
requirements.statement: The recipient of such a malformed request SHOULD use the 400 (Bad Request) status code.

requirements.title: Respond with 101 Switching Protocols
requirements.statement: The HTTP status code on the response MUST be 101 (Switching Protocols).

requirements.title: Include Connection header field value Upgrade in response
requirements.statement: The response SHALL include a Connection header field with value "Upgrade".

requirements.title: Include single Upgrade header field value connect-udp in response
requirements.statement: The response MUST include a single Upgrade header field with value "connect-udp".

requirements.title: Meet Capsule Protocol response requirements
requirements.statement: The response SHALL meet the requirements of HTTP responses that start the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Abort failed proxying attempts
requirements.statement: If any of these requirements are not met, the client MUST treat this proxying attempt as failed and abort the connection.

requirements.title: Send HTTP Setting
requirements.statement: Servers MUST send an HTTP Setting as specified in [EXT-CONNECT2] and [EXT-CONNECT3].
notes: Keeps the requirement scoped to the server-side setting and preserves the referenced extension specs.

requirements.title: Set :method to CONNECT
requirements.statement: The :method pseudo-header field MUST be "CONNECT".

requirements.title: Set :protocol to connect-udp
requirements.statement: The :protocol pseudo-header field MUST be "connect-udp".

requirements.title: Set :authority to the UDP proxy authority
requirements.statement: The :authority pseudo-header field MUST contain the authority of the UDP proxy.
notes: Keeps the authority source explicit and testable.

requirements.title: Require non-empty :path and :scheme
requirements.statement: The :path and :scheme pseudo-header fields MUST NOT be empty.
notes: Combines the paired non-empty constraint into one independently testable invariant.

requirements.title: Populate :path and :scheme from the URI Template
requirements.statement: Their values MUST contain the scheme and path from the URI Template after URI Template expansion completes.
notes: Trimmed for direct implementability while preserving the dependency on completed expansion.

requirements.title: Response status code in 2xx range
requirements.statement: The HTTP status code on the response MUST be in the 2xx (Successful) range.

requirements.title: Meet Capsule Protocol response requirements
requirements.statement: The response MUST meet the requirements of HTTP responses that start the Capsule Protocol; see Section 3.2 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Abort failed proxying attempts
requirements.statement: If any of these requirements are not met, the client MUST treat this proxying attempt as failed and abort the request.

requirements.title: Start HTTP Datagrams with Context ID
requirements.statement: All HTTP Datagrams associated with UDP Proxying request streams MUST start with a Context ID field.

requirements.title: Use 62-bit Context IDs
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be 62-bit integers in the range 0 to 2^62-1.

requirements.title: Encode Context IDs as varints
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be encoded as variable-length integers; see Section 16 of [QUIC].

requirements.title: Dynamically allocate non-zero Context IDs
requirements.statement: Non-zero Context ID values MUST be dynamically allocated.

requirements.title: Reserve Context ID 0 for UDP payloads
requirements.statement: The Context ID value of 0 MUST be reserved for UDP payloads.

requirements.title: Allocate even-numbered Context IDs on the client
requirements.statement: Non-zero even-numbered Context IDs MUST be client-allocated.

requirements.title: Allocate odd-numbered Context IDs on the proxy
requirements.statement: Odd-numbered Context IDs MUST be proxy-allocated.

requirements.title: Scope Context IDs per HTTP request
requirements.statement: The Context ID namespace MUST be tied to a given HTTP request.

requirements.title: Allow any allocation order for Context IDs
requirements.statement: Context IDs MAY be allocated in any order.

requirements.title: Do not re-allocate Context IDs in a namespace
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST NOT be re-allocated within a given HTTP namespace.

requirements.title: Allow allocated Context IDs to be used by any client or UDP proxy
requirements.statement: Once a Context ID has been allocated, any client or UDP proxy MAY use it regardless of which endpoint initially allocated it.

requirements.title: Permit future Context ID registration mechanisms
requirements.statement: Future extensions MAY use HTTP header fields or capsules to register Context IDs.

requirements.title: Context ID follows Quarter Stream ID in QUIC DATAGRAM frames
requirements.statement: When HTTP Datagrams are encoded using QUIC DATAGRAM frames, the Context ID field MUST directly follow the Quarter Stream ID field.

requirements.title: UDP Proxying HTTP Datagram Payload layout
requirements.statement: The UDP Proxying HTTP Datagram Payload MUST contain a Context ID field followed by a UDP Proxying Payload field.

requirements.title: Unknown Context ID handling
requirements.statement: If an HTTP/3 Datagram carrying an unknown Context ID is received, the receiver SHALL either drop it silently or buffer it temporarily for about a round trip while awaiting registration of the corresponding Context ID.

requirements.title: UDP Proxying Payload may be empty
requirements.statement: The UDP Proxying Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: UDP packets use Context ID zero
requirements.statement: UDP packets MUST be encoded using HTTP Datagrams with Context ID zero.

requirements.title: Context ID zero carries unmodified UDP payload
requirements.statement: When Context ID is zero, the UDP Proxying Payload field MUST contain the unmodified payload of a UDP packet.

requirements.title: Prohibit oversized HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT send HTTP Datagrams with a UDP Proxying Payload longer than 65527 bytes when Context ID is zero.

requirements.title: Abort streams for oversized received datagrams
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives an HTTP Datagram with Context ID zero and a UDP Proxying Payload longer than 65527 bytes MUST abort the corresponding stream.

requirements.title: Discard oversized datagrams when MTU is known
requirements.statement: A UDP proxy that knows its outgoing UDP packet length is limited by the underlying link MTU MUST discard incoming HTTP Datagrams with Context ID zero and a UDP Proxying Payload longer than that limit.

requirements.title: Discard DATAGRAM capsules for discarded datagrams
requirements.statement: If the discarded HTTP Datagram was transported by a DATAGRAM capsule, the receiver SHOULD discard the capsule without buffering its contents.

requirements.title: Handle early HTTP Datagrams by drop or temporary buffering
requirements.statement: If a UDP proxy receives an HTTP Datagram before the corresponding request, it SHALL either drop it silently or buffer it temporarily for about one round trip while awaiting the request.

requirements.title: Apply buffering limits to buffered datagrams
requirements.statement: Receivers that buffer datagrams SHOULD apply buffering limits to reduce the risk of resource exhaustion.

requirements.title: Allow optimistic datagram sending before response
requirements.statement: A client MAY send UDP packets in HTTP Datagrams before receiving the response to its UDP proxying request.

requirements.title: Avoid increasing UDP burstiness
requirements.statement: UDP proxies SHOULD avoid increasing burstiness of UDP traffic.

requirements.title: Do not queue packets to increase batching
requirements.statement: UDP proxies SHOULD NOT queue packets to increase batching.

requirements.title: Do not disable congestion control without certainty
requirements.statement: The underlying HTTP connection MUST NOT disable congestion control unless it has an out-of-band way of knowing with absolute certainty that the inner traffic is congestion-controlled.

requirements.title: Do not signal ECN support when congestion control is disabled
requirements.statement: If a client or UDP proxy with a connection containing a UDP Proxying request stream disables congestion control, it MUST NOT signal Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) support on that connection.

requirements.title: Mark IP headers Not-ECT when congestion control is disabled
requirements.statement: If a client or UDP proxy with a connection containing a UDP Proxying request stream disables congestion control, it MUST mark all IP headers with the Not-ECT codepoint.

requirements.title: Allow ECN feedback reporting when permitted
requirements.statement: It MAY continue to report ECN feedback via QUIC ACK_ECN frames or the TCP ECE bit, as the peer may not have disabled congestion control.

requirements.title: Prefer HTTP/3 for UDP proxying
requirements.statement: UDP proxying SHOULD be performed over HTTP/3 to allow leveraging the QUIC DATAGRAM frame.

requirements.title: Transmit UDP payloads in QUIC DATAGRAM frames
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/3 with the QUIC Datagram extension, UDP payloads MUST be transmitted in QUIC DATAGRAM frames.
notes: Single testable invariant; no cross-unit merge needed.

requirements.title: Limit QUIC DATAGRAM payload size
requirements.statement: QUIC DATAGRAM frames MUST carry UDP payloads only up to a length determined by the QUIC connection configuration and the Path MTU (PMTU).
notes: Single bounded behavior; no split needed.

requirements.title: Do not capsule oversized UDP payloads
requirements.statement: If a UDP proxy is using QUIC DATAGRAM frames and it receives a UDP payload from the target that will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the UDP proxy SHOULD NOT send the UDP payload in a DATAGRAM capsule.
notes: Advisory behavior is already isolated to one invariant.

requirements.title: Drop UDP payload in this scenario
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy SHOULD drop the UDP payload.
notes: Split from a compound sentence that also requires ICMP generation.

requirements.title: Send ICMP Packet Too Big to target in this scenario
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy SHOULD send an ICMP Packet Too Big message to the target.
notes: Split from a compound sentence that also requires dropping the payload.

requirements.title: No inner IP header in UDP proxying tunnels
requirements.statement: UDP proxying tunnels MUST NOT include an inner IP header.

requirements.title: Clients cannot control ECN codepoints on proxied UDP packets
requirements.statement: The UDP proxy MUST retain control of the ECN codepoints on UDP packets it sends to the target.

requirements.title: UDP proxies cannot communicate per-packet markings to clients
requirements.statement: UDP proxies MUST NOT communicate per-packet markings from the target to the UDP proxy.

requirements.title: Ignore ECN bits received from target
requirements.statement: A UDP proxy MUST ignore ECN bits in the IP header of UDP packets received from the target.

requirements.title: Set ECN bits to Not-ECT on outbound UDP packets
requirements.statement: A UDP proxy MUST set the ECN bits to Not-ECT on UDP packets it sends to the target.

requirements.title: Disallow UDP proxying to vulnerable targets
requirements.statement: UDP proxies MUST disallow UDP proxying requests to vulnerable targets, such as the proxy's own addresses and localhost, link-local, multicast, and broadcast addresses.

requirements.title: Use destination_ip_prohibited when rejecting disallowed requests
requirements.statement: UDP proxies MAY use the destination_ip_prohibited Proxy Error Type from Section 2.3.5 of PROXY-STATUS when rejecting such requests.
